clue.text: Gutless Swiss caught by sword remains petrified?

indicators.note: the sword catches the other letters and holds them inside it

parts.note: a foil is a light fencing sword

indicators.note: a gutless word has its insides removed, leaving only its first and last letters

parts.note: the first and last letters of Swiss, once its middle is taken out

explanation.surface: A cowardly Swiss is skewered by a blade and left frozen with fear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'petrified' looks like 'terrified', but the definition reads as remains turned to stone; 'Gutless' and 'caught by' do the work on the Swiss and the sword.
explanation.definitionFit: A fossil is the preserved trace of an ancient plant or animal, often turned into stone.

clue.text: Acceptable target in 'Test Your Strength' or 'Hook a Duck'?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a person or thing that may reasonably be attacked or criticised
second meaning, read literally: these are games at a funfair, a fair

explanation.surface: Fairground stalls are mocked as easy pickings for a critic.
explanation.walkthrough: Test Your Strength (hit a pad with a mallet) and Hook a Duck (fish plastic ducks from a trough) are traditional British funfair stalls.
explanation.definitionFit: Fair game is an idiom for someone open to legitimate ridicule, and literally a game played at a fair.

clue.text: Counterfeit note of debtor banked by team

indicators.note: the team's name forms banks on either side, enclosing the note

parts.note: Spurs is the nickname of Tottenham Hotspur football club
an IOU is a written note acknowledging a debt

explanation.surface: A forged IOU is deposited in the bank by a football club.
explanation.walkthrough: 'banked by' suggests money going into an account, but it means flanked, the team's name on both sides. Spurs is Tottenham Hotspur's nickname.
explanation.definitionFit: Spurious means false or not genuine, which is what a counterfeit article is.

clue.text: A little bonsai on Asian island

indicators.note: only a little part of the following words is used, a run of letters inside them

parts.note: the letters run across the words: bonsaI ON Asian

explanation.surface: A small dwarf tree sits on display somewhere in Asia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Asian island' reads as one phrase, but 'Asian' is part of the hiding place, and 'A little' points to a run of letters within: bonsaI ON Asian. Iona is a small island in the Scottish Hebrides.
explanation.definitionFit: Iona is an island in the Inner Hebrides, famous for its early Christian abbey.

clue.text: Lovely top mark realistic, first in Russian bagged

parts.note: A is the highest grade on a school paper

indicators.note: the realistic word bags, holds in, the Russian initial

parts.note: doable means realistic, achievable

indicators.note: only the first letter of Russian is used

parts.note: the first letter of Russian

explanation.surface: A Russian student gets a top grade for a lovely, realistic piece of work.
explanation.walkthrough: A, then DOABLE with the R from 'first in Russian' 'bagged' inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Adorable means delightful and charming, close to lovely as a term of praise.

clue.text: Double jeopardy has caught people almost entirely off guard, initially

indicators.note: jeopardy's word catches the rest and holds it inside

parts.note: danger is a synonym for jeopardy

indicators.note: off means out of order, so the shortened people is rearranged
all of the word except its last letter

parts.note: taken as written before it is cut and jumbled

indicators.note: the first letter of guard is used

parts.note: the first letter of guard

explanation.surface: Legal double jeopardy has trapped people who were caught off guard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Double jeopardy' looks like the legal term, but 'Double' is the definition. PEOPLE 'almost entirely' is PEOPL, 'off' jumbles it to OPPEL, 'initially' adds G from guard, and DANGER 'has caught' the lot.
explanation.definitionFit: A doppelganger is a person's double, a lookalike, from German for double-goer.

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to shake or sway, as an earthquake does
second meaning: a ... can be a small stone

explanation.surface: Shake a little stone.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a verb for shaking something to and fro and a noun for a stone.

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils
an eagle is a large bird of prey

explanation.surface: A dark-feathered bird of prey goes hunting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Black bird' suggests a blackbird, but it is B plus EAGLE.
explanation.definitionFit: A beagle is a hound bred for hunting hares, so it is a hunting dog.

clue.text: Old rotten tree in West Country city

parts.note: ex means former, old, as in ex-wife

indicators.note: something rotten falls apart, so the letters of tree are rearranged

explanation.surface: An ancient decaying tree stands in a south-western cathedral city.
explanation.walkthrough: EX, then 'rotten' turns TREE into ETER. The West Country is the south-west of England; Exeter is the county town of Devon.
explanation.definitionFit: Exeter is a cathedral city in Devon, in the region of England called the West Country.

clue.text: Animal is generally undernourished, and needing affection primarily

indicators.note: primarily means first of all, so the opening letter of each of these words is used

parts.words: is generally undernourished, and needing affection
parts.note: the initials of these six words

explanation.surface: A neglected pet that is hungry and needs some love.
explanation.walkthrough: 'primarily' takes the initials of 'is generally undernourished, and needing affection'.
explanation.definitionFit: An iguana is a large lizard of tropical America, an animal sometimes kept as a pet.

indicators.note: the wise word welcomes the step in, holding it inside

parts.note: sage means wise
a pace is a single step

explanation.surface: A modern idea is warmly received by a sage.
explanation.definitionFit: Space-age describes something very modern, up to date with current technology.

clue.text: Let your hair down more, chaps, little time for feeling of uncertainty!

parts.note: to let your hair down is to be wild, so doing it more is to be wilder
men are chaps
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A cheerful invitation for the lads to party harder, with time running short.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Let your hair down more' is read as BE WILDER, then MEN and T.
explanation.definitionFit: Bewilderment is a state of confusion, of not knowing what is happening.

definitions.meaning: second meaning: small particles of stone or sand

explanation.surface: Is courage found in tiny pieces?
explanation.definitionFit: Grit means both resolve under pressure and fine granules of stone.

indicators.note: the word goes back, read from end to start

parts.note: a revel is a lively celebration

explanation.surface: A party at the pub goes wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bar' suggests a pub, but it is a metal bar; REVEL 'backfires' to give the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A lever is a rigid bar used to prise or lift things.

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a ... steak is cooked only briefly, barely seared
second meaning: ... jokes are rude or obscene

explanation.surface: Something exceptionally unusual and also rude.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Very rare' reads as 'scarce', but it is a steak-cooking term.
explanation.definitionFit: The colour word describes steak seared for seconds and humour that is smutty.

indicators.note: the star pins the one in place, holding it inside

parts.note: a star is a luminary, a famous person
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: One person is caught out by a celebrity on the steps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nailed by' puts I inside STAR.
explanation.definitionFit: A stair is a single step in a staircase.

parts.note: man is slang address, like dude
a go is a try or attempt

explanation.surface: An offer to a pal to taste some fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: A mango is a sweet tropical fruit with orange flesh.

clue.text: Stuck in ditch, an outing ruined for climber

indicators.note: the anagram is stuck inside the ditch's word

parts.note: a moat is a ditch round a castle

indicators.note: a ruined outing is wrecked, so the letters of an and outing are rearranged

explanation.surface: A day trip is spoilt when the party gets stuck in a ditch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ruined' rearranges AN OUTING into UNTAINGO, which is 'Stuck in' MOAT.
explanation.definitionFit: The mountain goat is famed as a sure-footed animal that scales steep cliffs.

definitions.meaning: first meaning, read cryptically: mono is one and a rail is a line, so a single-line railway

explanation.walkthrough: The first sense is playful: a monorail is a train that runs on one line.
explanation.definitionFit: The answer is a brief joke told in a sentence, and humorously a train on a single track.

indicators.note: the letters of alarming shift around into a new order

explanation.surface: A frightening change of position that is open to question.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of 'Alarming' are shifted.
explanation.definitionFit: A marginal case is borderline, so it is open to argument either way.

clue.text: Name in heading dead stupid, reason kept secret

indicators.note: something stupid is muddled, so all these letters are jumbled together

explanation.surface: A title in a headline is dead wrong, and the real motive is hidden.
explanation.walkthrough: N goes 'in' with HEADING and DEAD, and 'stupid' rearranges the whole pool.
explanation.definitionFit: A hidden agenda is a concealed motive behind someone's actions.

parts.note: split it as super, an old British exclamation of approval, and sorcerer, a magician; one word means both

explanation.walkthrough: Read the single word as two: 'super' and 'sorcerer'. As an adjective the answer is dated British slang for excellent.
explanation.definitionFit: A wizard is a magician, and 'wizard!' was once schoolboy slang meaning marvellous.

clue.text: Empty sheet, paper for school class

indicators.note: an empty word has its insides removed, keeping only the first and last letters

parts.note: the outer letters of sheet, once emptied of its middle
a ream is a quantity of paper, 500 sheets

explanation.surface: A blank page and a stack of stationery for the classroom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Empty' leaves ST from SHEET, then REAM. In British schools a stream is a group of pupils of similar ability.
explanation.definitionFit: A stream is a set of pupils grouped by ability within a year of a school.

indicators.note: the two words switch places, swapping the letters around

explanation.surface: Keen on flicking a device on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'switching it on' sounds like turning on a device, but IT and ON are swapped.
explanation.definitionFit: Being into something is informal for being keen on it.

indicators.note: a tangled thread is twisted out of order, so the letters of fibre are rearranged

explanation.surface: A short strand of thread gets knotted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in a tangle' rearranges the letters of FIBRE.
explanation.definitionFit: Brief means short in time or length.

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a gulp of strong drink
second meaning: to hit them hard

explanation.surface: Drink punch, the fruity cocktail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drink punch' reads as an instruction to sip a cocktail, but the two words are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a swig of spirits and a heavy blow.

parts.note: on means working, as a machine that is on

explanation.surface: A figure still in operation at twelve.
explanation.definitionFit: Noon is twelve o'clock midday.

parts.note: a hug is a cuddle

explanation.surface: Give an aged writer an embrace.
explanation.walkthrough: 'old author' looks like one phrase, but 'old' gives O.
explanation.definitionFit: Victor Hugo was the French author of Les Misérables.

indicators.note: the jumbled names include the individual, holding it inside
the letters of names are changed into a new order

parts.note: one means a single individual

explanation.surface: Botanists rename plants, one at a time.
explanation.definitionFit: Anemones are flowering plants of the buttercup family, also called windflowers.

clue.text: Unknown number visiting European city retire

indicators.note: the number visits the city, going inside it

parts.note: Turin is a city in northern Italy
N stands for an unknown number in algebra

explanation.surface: A mystery figure on a trip to Italy decides to retire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'visiting' puts N into TURIN. 'retire' is to go to bed, not to stop working.
explanation.definitionFit: To turn in is an idiom for going to bed for the night, retiring.

clue.text: Party elected to punch crony, bully

parts.note: a do is a party

indicators.note: to punch is to pierce through, so the elected word goes inside the crony

parts.note: a mate is a friend, a crony
in means elected, as a party voted in

explanation.surface: A party man elected to office hits his friend, the bully.
explanation.walkthrough: 'punch' looks like violence in the surface, but here it means pierce: one word goes through the middle of another.
explanation.definitionFit: To dominate is to control others by force of will, as a bully does.

clue.text: Pen top on rubber in shade of pink

indicators.note: the first letter of rubber goes inside the pink word

parts.note: coral is a pinkish-orange colour

indicators.note: the top, first letter, of rubber

parts.note: the first letter of rubber

explanation.surface: A pen with a rubber on the end, coloured pink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pen' suggests a writing tool with an eraser, but it is an animal enclosure. 'top on' rubber gives R, which goes 'in' CORAL.
explanation.definitionFit: A corral is an enclosure for livestock, a pen for horses or cattle.
